title: Companywide Governance Toolkit: Policies, Procedures, and Templates
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This toolkit consolidates company-wide policies and standard processes for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended to provide a single reference for compliance, onboarding, and operational consistency across Redwood Inference.

Audience:
Employees, managers, IT, Security, Finance, Legal, and People Ops.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood corporate entities and to contractors with accounts or integrations into Redwood systems, except where an explicit customer contract or regulatory constraint specifies different controls (see 'Exceptions' below).

Principles

- Least privilege by default: grant the minimum access required for each role and task.
- Auditability: all privileged actions must be traceable in logs retained according to the Data Retention Schedule.
- Standardized approvals: approvals should be recorded in Jira/Service Desk or the designated procurement tool.
- Segregation of duties: procurement, approval, and reconciliation roles must be separated for high-value purchases.
- Risk-based vendor decisions: vendor onboarding requires proportional security and privacy review.

Key Contacts

- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team)
- Access requests: Identity & Access Management (IAM) team (iam-team@redwood.example.com)
- Procurement requests: Procurement Queue (procurement@redwood.example.com)
- Security assessments: InfoSec (infosec@redwood.example.com)

1) Access & Permissions

Overview:
Central SSO: Okta is the canonical identity provider. All user access to corporate apps must be provisioned through Okta or an approved SCIM integration.

Roles & Access Types:
- Employee: standard corporate accounts (email, Slack, Jira, Confluence).
- Contractor: time-limited accounts with sponsor and expiration.
- Privileged operator: elevated rights for infra and runtime services. Requires just-in-time (JIT) approval.
- Service account: non-human identity for automation; use short-lived keys where possible.

Access Request & Approval Flow (standard):
1. Submit access request in Jira Service Desk using the "access-request" template.
2. Auto-provision based on group mappings when applicable. Unmapped requests route to IAM for manual review.
3. Sponsor (manager or team lead) must approve within 3 business days.
4. IAM provisions account and records change in audit log (GCP/AWS project).

Periodic Review:
- Quarterly access review for all groups with privileged access.
- Contract/contractor accounts are reviewed monthly and automatically expire unless renewed.

Privilege Escalation & Emergency Access:
- Emergency break-glass is available for PagerDuty responders; requests must be annotated and followed by a post-incident review.
- All emergency elevations are time-limited (default 4 hours) and require a ticket and retrospective.

Technical Controls:
- MFA required for all human accounts.
- Passwords and secrets stored in HashiCorp Vault.
- JIT privileged access via Vault/Okta integrated workflow.

2) Change Management

Change Categories:
- Standard (repeatable, pre-authorized): configuration changes, routine deployments.
- Normal (requires CAB): infra upgrades, schema migrations, config changes that affect multiple services.
- Emergency: fixes required to restore service or mitigate active incidents.

Change Windows & Scheduling:
- Regular maintenance window: Thursdays 02:00–05:00 UTC for non-critical infra changes.
- Major releases must be scheduled with at least 72 hours' notice and a rollout plan.

Change Request Procedure (normal change):
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in Jira with the "change-request-template". Include risk assessment and rollback plan.
2. Notify affected owners and stakeholders at least 48 hours before change.
3. CAB review for medium/high risk changes (CAB meets Tuesdays 16:00 UTC).
4. If approved, implement during agreed window with live monitoring.
5. Post-change verification and update the CR with outcome and metrics.

Emergency Change Procedure:
1. Emergency change initiated via PagerDuty incident link and must include owner and rollback plan.
2. Implement only the minimal fix required.
3. Document change in Jira within 24 hours and schedule a post-incident review.

Rollbacks & Safeguards:
- All changes must include an automated rollback plan where practicable.
- Canary rollouts or feature flags required for changes that affect user-facing outputs.

3) Data Management & Classification

Classification Levels:
- Public: Intended for public release. No special controls required.
- Internal: Company-internal business information. Access limited to employees and contractors.
- Confidential: Customer data, financials, strategic product plans. Requires strict access control and encryption at rest and in transit.
- Restricted: Highly sensitive PII, regulated data, or keys. Requires additional approvals and restricted hosting options.

Handling Rules Summary (table):
| Classification | Storage | Transmission | Retention | Example |
|---------------|---------|--------------|----------|---------|
| Public | Any | Any | 1 year | Blog posts, marketing assets |
| Internal | Encrypted storage | TLS | 3 years | Internal plans, meeting notes |
| Confidential | Encrypted (KMS-managed) | TLS + IAM | 7 years or contractual | Customer data, contracts |
| Restricted | Encrypted (HSM/KMS), access request | TLS + VPN | Per contract/regulation | PII, keys, health data |

Data Access Requests:
- Data extraction requests must use the Data Access Request template and be routed through the Data Governance mailbox (data-governance@redwood.example.com).
- Approvals for Confidential/Restricted exports require Infosec and Data Owner sign-off.

Retention & Deletion:
- All data retention schedules are defined in the Data Retention Matrix (link in related pages).
- Deletion requests from users/customers are handled according to the Privacy Policy and processed within 30 days unless subject to legal hold.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Procurement Thresholds and Approvals:
- <$5,000: Team lead approval; charge to departmental card.
- $5,000–$50,000: Procurement + Finance approval required; three quotes recommended for hardware vendors.
- >$50,000: Executive sponsor plus Legal review and signed contract required.

Preferred Tools & Flows:
- Purchase requests via Procurify (or procurement Jira queue).
- Corporate cards: managed through Ramp; expense submit via Ramp + Concur expense entry for external reimbursements.

Expense Policy Highlights:
- Per diem and travel allowances follow the Travel Policy section; corporate card receipts must be uploaded within 7 days of transaction.
- Entertainment expenses require attendee list and business purpose.
- Personal purchases on corporate card are prohibited and must be reimbursed immediately.

Procurement Checklist (before issuing PO):
- Confirm budget and cost center.
- Security questionnaire for any SaaS vendor (automated via vendor onboarding).
- Data residency requirements confirmed if vendor will process Confidential or Restricted data.

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding Steps:
1. Vendor intake form submitted via Procurement Queue.
2. Initial legal and finance checks (tax forms, W-8/W-9 equivalents).
3. Security and privacy questionnaire (scored). Vendors scoring <70 require compensating controls or a remediation plan.
4. Contracting and SLA negotiation.
5. Procurement issues PO and registers vendor in Supplier Registry.

Security Requirements:
- Vendors processing Confidential or Restricted data must provide SOC 2 Type II or equivalent evidence, or complete a compensating controls assessment.
- Encryption and key management expectations documented in vendor contract.

Periodic Review:
- High-risk vendors reviewed annually; medium-risk vendors reviewed every 18 months.

Termination & Offboarding:
- Include data return/destruction, transition assistance, and certificate of destruction where applicable.
- Revoke all service accounts and rotate shared secrets in coordination with IAM.

6) Travel Policy (Summary)

Booking & Approval:
- All travel > $1,000 requires manager approval and entry into Travel Request in Concur.
- Preferred vendors and negotiated rates should be used where available.

Allowances:
- Economy or equivalent for flights < 6 hours; premium economy for flights 6–10 hours; business class requires Director-level approval.
- Per diem for meals varies by city tier and is published in the Travel Rates table.

Safety & Incident Reporting:
- Employees traveling to higher-risk locations must register travel plans with People Ops and subscribe to security advisories.
- Security incidents while traveling must be reported to Security immediately and documented in the incident system.

7) Internal Templates & Examples

Canonical templates (available in the Templates folder):
- change-request-template (Jira): fields: summary, impacted-systems, owner, risk-level, rollback-plan, test-plan.
- access-request-template (Jira): fields: requester, sponsor, requested-groups, justification, expiration-date.
- vendor-security-questionnaire-template (Google Form/PDF).
- procurement-purchase-order (Procurify JSON + PDF stub).
- expense-claim-template (Concur fields + receipts checklist).
- data-access-request-template (Confluence form): includes justification, export scope, retention, approvers.

Examples & Snippets:
- Example rollback script (bash):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  # revert to previous image tag
  kubectl set image deployment/api api=registry.redwood.example.com/api:$PREV_TAG -n prod

- Example change request summary (good):
  "Deploy model-serving v2.3.1 with canary 10% traffic for 2 hours; health checks target latency <= 150ms; rollback to v2.3.0 on error threshold > 2% 5xx for 10m."

Governance & Review Cycle

- This toolkit is reviewed yearly by Finance & Legal with input from Security and IAM.
- Ad-hoc updates may be issued for regulatory changes or observed process failures.

Exceptions

- Exceptions to these policies require a documented Risk Exception Request, signed by Policy Owner and the appropriate executive. All exceptions are recorded in the Exceptions Register.

Appendix: Enforcement & Metrics

Key metrics tracked quarterly:
- Number of privileged accounts and percent with MFA enforced (target: 100% for humans).
- Mean time to provision access (target: <= 3 business days).
- Percentage of vendor security questionnaires returned (target: 95% for new vendors).
- Percentage of changes with automated rollback plan (target: 90%).

Non-compliance:
- Policy violations are handled per HR disciplinary process for employees and up to contract termination for vendors. Security incidents escalate per the Incident Response Process.

Revision history:
- 2025-03-12: Initial consolidation (Maya Chen).
- 2025-08-20: Added JIT access controls and vendor scoring thresholds (Infosec review).
- 2026-01-15: Updated procurement thresholds and travel allowances (Finance & People Ops).
